Characteristics: Color: Salajit Chitrali is typically dark brown or black, and sometimes it can appear glossy or shiny. Texture: It has a thick, tar-like consistency when fresh but can become more solid when cooled. Taste: It is known to have a bitter and earthy taste. Aroma: The resin has a strong, pungent smell, often described as a mixture of earth and minerals. Composition: Salajit Chitrali is rich in minerals, fulvic acid, and humic acid. Enhancing sexual health: It has been traditionally used as a natural aphrodisiac and to treat male infertility and low libido. Supporting immune function: It may help strengthen the immune system and combat infections. Anti-aging properties: Its antioxidant-rich composition is believed to help reduce the effects of aging and support healthy skin. Usage: Salajit Chitrali is typically consumed in small amounts, either by dissolving it in warm water, milk, or tea.
